plan.name: L4-L5 Post-Herniation Reconditioning — 2-Week Starter Block
plan.description: A conservative 2-week introductory strength block for a 42-year-old male with a resolved L4-L5 disc herniation. No heavy spinal loading; no loaded spinal flexion. Focuses on hip-hinge patterning, anti-flexion core stability, horizontal push/pull, and single-leg work. Designed to precede a full 12-week programme once tolerance is confirmed.

goals.name: Re-establish safe movement patterns
goals.description: Groove hip-hinge, squat, and anti-flexion core patterns with zero pain provocation.

goals.name: Build foundational strength
goals.description: Develop moderate lower and upper body strength within spinal-safe loading parameters.

phases.name: Phase 1 — Movement Foundations
phases.description: Two weeks of low-load, high-quality movement. RPE capped at 6/10. Emphasis on technique, bracing, and pain-free range of motion. Three sessions per week on non-consecutive days.

exercises.name: Cat-Camel (neutral only — stop at neutral, no end-range flexion)

days.name: Session B — Upper Body Push & Pull

activities.name: Pallof Press (Cable) — add 1 sec pause at extension

days.name: Session B — Upper Body Push & Pull (progressive)

activities.name: Trainer check-in: pain score, movement quality review, readiness for Phase 2 loading

checkpoints.name: 2-Week Block Review

measurements.note: Pain score (0-10) during and 24h after each session
Movement quality rating by trainer: goblet squat, RDL, bird dog

questions: Any pain or neurological symptoms (numbness, tingling) during or after sessions?
How is sleep quality and general energy?
Confident to progress to Phase 2 loading?

notifications.message: Stop immediately and contact your trainer if you experience any sharp back pain, leg pain, numbness, or tingling during any exercise.
